clue.text: Treatment of many in an ACAS concern

indicators.note: the word 'in' tells us the letter for 'many' goes inside the ACAS phrase

parts.note: ACAS, the UK conciliation service, is concerned with mediation in disputes
C is the Roman numeral for 100, a crossword stand-in for many

explanation.surface: A conciliation body deals with how to treat a large workforce.
explanation.walkthrough: ACAS (Advisory, Conciliation and Arbitration Service) is the British body that steps into industrial disputes; its business is mediation.
explanation.definitionFit: Medicine given to a patient is a form of treatment.

clue.text: Pronounced fit for consumption

indicators.note: 'pronounced' says the word is taken as heard, not as spelt

parts.note: meet is an old word for fit or suitable

explanation.surface: Declared good enough to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: Meat is flesh eaten as food, something for consumption.

clue.text: Customs to which Frederick was a slave

definitions.meaning: customs is the tax levied on imports

definitions.text: to which Frederick was a slave
definitions.meaning: Frederic in Gilbert and Sullivan's The Pirates of Penzance is the 'slave of ...'

explanation.surface: Border officials meet an operetta hero bound by obligation.
explanation.definitionFit: Duty is tax on imports; Frederic is bound by obligation to the pirates.

clue.text: Monster in car to be destroyed in the compound

indicators.note: 'in' places the monster inside the wrecked letters
'destroyed' says the words are wrecked and rebuilt in a new order

parts.note: the Hydra is the many-headed monster of Greek myth

explanation.surface: A beast inside a car that is about to be wrecked in a yard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'destroyed' rearranges the three words into CARBOTE; 'in' then sets the monster within those letters. The surface pictures a scrapyard, but 'compound' is the chemistry sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Sugars and starches are organic compounds of carbon, hydrogen and oxygen.

clue.text: Walk the ship

definitions.meaning: to walk heavily or a long way
a cargo ship with no fixed route

explanation.surface: Someone is told to walk the ship.
explanation.definitionFit: To tramp is to trudge; a tramp steamer is a cargo vessel without a regular route.

clue.text: Decree for one in the artillery

indicators.note: 'in' places the numeral inside the word for artillery

parts.note: ordnance is military artillery and its supplies
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A ruling is made for a gunner.
explanation.definitionFit: An ordinance is an official order or regulation.

clue.text: Warriors' claim to be religious

parts.note: saying 'I am' is how one claims to be something, contracted to I'M
PI is short for pious, so religious

explanation.surface: Fighters boast of their own piety.
explanation.definitionFit: An impi is a Zulu regiment, a body of fighting men.

clue.text: I'm at a ruin — a broken-down ' place in Africa

indicators.note: 'broken-down' says the letters fall apart and rebuild as something else

explanation.surface: A traveller laments a shabby, crumbling spot in Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Mauritania is a country in north-west Africa.

clue.text: Not aware of being sent in first to one kind of specialist

indicators.note: 'first' places the word 'in' ahead of the word sent

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one
ENT is ear, nose and throat, a medical specialism

explanation.surface: Unaware of being referred first to a consultant.
explanation.definitionFit: Something insentient has no feeling or consciousness, so cannot perceive.

clue.text: Following a course without charge

indicators.note: 'without' in its old sense of outside: the course wraps around the charge

parts.note: afters is British slang for the pudding course of a meal
a ward is someone placed in another's charge

explanation.surface: Taking a class for which no fee is asked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without charge' reads as free of cost, but 'without' here is the old word for outside, so the course goes around the charge. AFTERS is British slang for pudding.
explanation.definitionFit: Following in time means later, at a subsequent point.

clue.text: Birds the Cockney offers for sale, we hear

indicators.note: 'we hear' says the word is judged by how it is spoken

parts.note: offers for sale is hawks; a Cockney drops the H, giving 'awks

explanation.surface: A London street trader sells birds.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney is the working-class London accent, famous for dropping the initial H.
explanation.definitionFit: Auks are diving seabirds such as puffins and guillemots.

clue.text: Churchman is in agreement over the admission of a saint

annotationWithheld.why: Churchman is in agreement over the admission of a saint (12), CANONISATION: CANON + IS is clear, but no reading of 'in agreement over' yields ATION (AT ONE gives one letter too many), and no source gives the parse
annotationWithheld.clue: Churchman is in agreement over the admission of a saint

clue.text: Company representative almost feeling satisfaction

parts.note: an MP, Member of Parliament, is an elected representative

indicators.note: 'almost' says the word for feeling is not given in full, losing one letter

parts.note: a sensation is a feeling

explanation.surface: A firm's agent nearly feels content.
explanation.walkthrough: Here 'almost' takes the first S off SENSATION, leaving ENSATION.
explanation.definitionFit: Compensation is the redress that gives an injured party satisfaction for a loss.

clue.text: Collision to cause huff to English driver

indicators.note: a collision smashes things together, so these letters are jumbled up

explanation.surface: A crash makes a motorist go off in a sulk.
explanation.definitionFit: A chauffeuse is a woman employed to drive a car.

clue.text: No-account dentist, perhaps, but he tells a good tale

indicators.note: 'perhaps' suggests the letters might be ordered differently

parts.note: O is nothing (no) and AC is account

explanation.surface: A worthless dentist may nonetheless spin a good yarn.
explanation.walkthrough: O for no plus AC for account, mixed with DENTIST, make the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A raconteur of short amusing stories is someone who tells a good yarn.

clue.text: Sweetheart takes money order on joint holiday

parts.note: honey is a term of endearment for a sweetheart

explanation.surface: A lover pays by postal order for a shared vacation.
explanation.definitionFit: A honeymoon is the holiday a newly married couple take together.

clue.text: Work with iron and gold for tyrant

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a work
to iron is to press
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: Doing chores with an iron and gold for a despot.
explanation.definitionFit: A tyrant rules cruelly and harshly, crushing people.

clue.text: The beast may write, say, a letter

parts.note: 'write' spoken is 'right', and all right is OK; 'say' flags the spoken sense
pi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: An animal is supposedly able to put pen to paper.
explanation.definitionFit: The okapi is a forest animal of central Africa related to the giraffe.

clue.text: The pain it causes can be cruel

indicators.note: 'can be' says these letters can be made into another word by rearranging

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that the pain from something can be cruel.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is read loosely: the answer is the thing behind the pain mentioned.
explanation.definitionFit: A stomach sore is a classic source of gnawing pain.

clue.text: Sketch most of the island with accuracy

parts.note: a precis is a brief sketch or summary

indicators.note: 'most of' tells us to drop the final letter of the island

parts.note: Iona is a Scottish island in the Inner Hebrides

explanation.surface: Drawing much of an island with care.
explanation.walkthrough: IONA, a small island off western Scotland, loses its last letter to give ION.
explanation.definitionFit: Precision and accuracy both mean exactness.

clue.text: Nominal leader admits the king is without a real pioneer

indicators.note: 'admits' means the leader lets other letters in, so they sit inside

parts.note: a frontman is a figurehead, a leader in name only

indicators.note: 'without' in the sense of outside: IS goes around the king

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the monarch

explanation.surface: A figurehead accepts that the monarch lacks a true trailblazer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but is the old word for outside, giving IERS; 'admits' then puts that inside the figurehead. ER (Elizabeth Regina) is the crossword's usual monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A frontiersman lives on the edge of settled land, a genuine pioneer.

clue.text: Cane will make you smart

definitions.meaning: to cane is to strike with a stick

explanation.surface: A beating will teach you a painful lesson.
explanation.definitionFit: Swish is a stroke of a cane; swish also means stylish.

clue.text: Eyesore partly due to nasty effluent

indicators.note: 'partly' says only a portion of the following words is used

explanation.surface: An ugly sight is caused in part by foul discharge.
explanation.definitionFit: A sty is an inflamed swelling on the eyelid, literally a sore eye.

clue.text: Race for the trees

definitions.meaning: a classic horse race for fillies at Epsom

explanation.surface: Running a contest to save the forest.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oaks is an English Classic horse race; oaks are trees.

clue.text: A French appeal for one

parts.note: un is French for a
it is slang for sex appeal

explanation.surface: A French plea made for a single person.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit is a single thing, one of something.

clue.text: Plant of which a part is Di's perhaps

indicators.note: 'perhaps' suggests these words could be arranged some other way

explanation.surface: A garden plant, part of which is maybe Princess Diana's.
explanation.walkthrough: Di is a familiar short form of Diana.
explanation.definitionFit: The aspidistra is a hardy leafy pot plant, a Victorian parlour favourite.

clue.text: Artist causes girls to lose their heads

indicators.note: 'lose their heads' means the first letter of the girl's name goes

parts.note: girls named Betty, Hetty or Letty, any of which loses its first letter

explanation.surface: A painter makes young women be beheaded.
explanation.walkthrough: Several girls' names (Betty, Hetty, Letty) work, hence the plural.
explanation.definitionFit: William Etty was an English painter known for nudes.

clue.text: Port's for Michael and Gabriel, say

definitions.meaning: Archangel is a Russian port on the White Sea; with 's it reads as 'Archangel is'
Michael and Gabriel are senior angels in scripture

explanation.surface: A harbour town is named for two saints.
explanation.definitionFit: Archangel is a city name; archangels are chief angels, Michael and Gabriel being examples.
